newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan crude imports climb in November.
newsitem.headline: Japan crude imports climb in November.

text.p: Japan's crude oil imports in November rose 1.6 percent from the same month a year ago to 22.49 million kilolitres, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Wednesday.
Shipments from the United Arab Emirates, Japan's largest source of crude imports, rose 9.8 percent from a year earlier to 6.57 million kl.
Crude throughput totaled 20.74 million kl, up 1.7 percent from November 1995. It was the first year-on-year rise in three months, MITI said.
Saudi Arabia, the second biggest crude oil exporter to Japan, shipped 4.54 million kl, up 17.1 percent year-on-year. Iran followed with 3.08 million kl, up 38.8 percent.
Japan lifted 1.27 million kl from Kuwait, down 11 percent from November last year.
The Middle East was the source of 82.2 percent of Japan's oil imports in November.
Japan also imported a total of 2.18 million kilolitres of crude oil from Asia, down 20.4 percent from November last year.
Indonesia, which shipped about 1.07 million kl of crude oil, was the largest exporter of crude in Asia to Japan.
There were no crude oil imports from Africa in November.
